note: User-facing wording for diagnostic finding codes. Classification lives in anvil-diagnostics rules; this file never decides confidence. Placeholders use {name}.

local.invalid_url.title: The request URL is not valid
does_not_prove: That any server or gateway returned an error — no network activity happened.

remediation.text: Correct the URL or protocol in {field}.

local.unresolved_variable.title: A variable could not be resolved
local.unresolved_variable.explanation: Anvil stopped before sending because {message} Unresolved variables are never replaced with an empty value.
does_not_prove: That the credentials or the authorization server are at fault.

remediation.text: Define the variable in the selected environment, the workspace, the folder or the request, or fix its name.

confirm_with: Open the Effective request inspector to see which scopes were searched.

local.variable_cycle.title: Variables reference each other in a cycle
does_not_prove: Anything about the destination — nothing was sent.

remediation.text: Break the cycle so every variable eventually resolves to a literal value.

local.missing_attachment.title: A file used by the request is missing
does_not_prove: That the destination rejected the payload — it was never sent.

remediation.text: Re-link the file or attach it to the workspace so it travels with exports.

local.client_identity_invalid.title: The client certificate or private key could not be loaded
local.client_identity_invalid.explanation: Anvil could not use the selected client identity: {message}. No connection was attempted.
does_not_prove: That the server rejected a certificate — the key was never loaded or presented.

remediation.text: Re-import the certificate and an unencrypted PKCS#8, PKCS#1 or SEC1 key (or a PKCS#12 bundle with its password).

local.client_identity_key_mismatch.title: The private key does not match the client certificate
local.client_identity_key_mismatch.explanation: The selected private key belongs to a different public key than the certificate. Anvil refused to present this pair; nothing was sent.
does_not_prove: That the peer rejected the request — the handshake never started.

remediation.text: Select the private key that was issued with this certificate.

local.tls_profile_invalid.title: The TLS profile is not usable
local.tls_profile_invalid.explanation: Anvil could not build the TLS configuration: {message}. No connection was attempted.
does_not_prove: Anything about the destination's certificate.

remediation.text: Fix the CA bundle or trust settings in the TLS profile.

local.proxy_config_invalid.title: The proxy configuration is invalid
local.proxy_config_invalid.explanation: Anvil did not send the request: {message}
does_not_prove: That the destination or a gateway backend is down.

remediation.text: Correct the proxy profile address, type or credential reference.

local.lint_blocked.title: The body failed syntax validation
local.lint_blocked.explanation: {message} The request was not sent. Choose "Send anyway" to deliberately send an invalid body.
does_not_prove: That the destination would reject the body.

remediation.text: Fix the syntax error, or send anyway for a deliberate malformed-payload test.

local.unsupported_combination.title: These settings cannot be combined
local.unsupported_combination.explanation: {message} Anvil refuses unsupported combinations before sending instead of silently changing them.
does_not_prove: Anything about the destination.

remediation.text: Choose a supported protocol/transport combination for {field}.

local.auth_preparation_failed.title: Credentials could not be prepared
local.auth_preparation_failed.explanation: Anvil could not produce the configured credential before sending: {message}. The API request itself was not sent.
does_not_prove: That the destination API rejected a request it never received.

remediation.text: Check the auth profile settings and any token endpoint it depends on.

confirm_with: The execution log shows which credential step failed.

local.oauth_interaction_required.title: Sign in before sending with this OAuth profile
does_not_prove: That the destination API or a gateway rejected the request — it was never sent.
That the authorization server is unavailable — Anvil did not request a token with any other grant.

remediation.text: Use Sign in on the OAuth auth profile to authorize in your system browser, then send again.
If this API is meant for a non-interactive client, change the profile to the client-credentials grant deliberately.

confirm_with: The auth profile shows whether a token is cached for this workspace.

local.vault_locked.title: Anvil is locked
local.vault_locked.explanation: Secrets are unavailable while the vault is locked, so the request was not prepared or sent.

remediation.text: Unlock Anvil and send again.

local.request_too_large.title: The request body exceeds the local limit
does_not_prove: That any server enforces the same limit.

remediation.text: Reduce the body or raise the local request-body limit in settings.

local.validation_failed.title: The request could not be prepared
does_not_prove: That any remote component returned an error.

remediation.text: Correct {field} and send again.

local.response_limit_reached.title: Reading stopped at Anvil's response size limit
local.response_limit_reached.explanation: Response headers arrived with status {status}. Anvil stopped reading after {bytes} body bytes because its local maximum response size was reached. This is a local limit, not a fault of the peer.
does_not_prove: That the server sent a malformed or oversized response by its own rules.

remediation.text: Raise the maximum response size for this request if you need the full body.

client.dns.no_such_host.title: The host name does not exist (client DNS)
client.dns.no_such_host.explanation: Anvil's resolver reported that {host} does not exist. This happened on your side of the connection, before contacting any server or gateway.
alternatives: The name is misspelled.
The name exists only on a private/VPN DNS server this machine is not using.
A DNS override or custom resolver is sending queries to the wrong server.
does_not_prove: That a gateway failed to resolve its backend — the gateway was never contacted.

remediation.text: Check the host name and which resolver this machine or workspace uses.

confirm_with: Resolve the same name with the same resolver from this machine.

client.dns.no_records.title: The host name has no usable addresses
client.dns.no_records.explanation: {host} resolved, but no address of an acceptable type was returned ({message}).
alternatives: The name has only IPv6 (or only IPv4) records and the IP preference excludes them.
does_not_prove: That the destination service is down.

remediation.text: Check the DNS records and the IP family preference.

client.dns.timeout.title: Name resolution did not finish in time
client.dns.timeout.explanation: Resolving {host} did not complete within {deadline_ms} ms. The resolver did not answer; why is not known from this evidence.
alternatives: The DNS server is unreachable or overloaded.
A VPN or network change left a stale resolver configuration.
UDP DNS traffic is filtered.
does_not_prove: That the destination is down.
That the name does not exist.

remediation.text: Check resolver reachability from this machine, or use a DNS override for testing.

confirm_with: Query the same resolver directly and compare response times.

client.dns.server_failure.title: The DNS server could not answer
client.dns.server_failure.explanation: The resolver reported a temporary or server-side failure for {host} ({message}).
alternatives: The authoritative server is failing (SERVFAIL).
DNSSEC validation failed.
does_not_prove: That the name does not exist.

remediation.text: Retry later or check the resolver and the zone's authoritative servers.

client.dns.other.title: Name resolution failed
does_not_prove: Any specific DNS cause.

remediation.text: Check the host name and resolver configuration.

client.connect.refused.title: The connection was refused
client.connect.refused.explanation: The peer at {host} actively refused the TCP connection. Nothing was sent.
alternatives: Nothing is listening on that port.
A firewall rejects (rather than drops) the connection.
The service is restarting.
does_not_prove: That a process crashed.
That a gateway's backend failed — this is the connection from Anvil itself.

remediation.text: Check the host and port, and whether the service/listener is running.

confirm_with: Check the listener on the target host (e.g. with ss/netstat).

client.connect.timeout.title: The connection was not established in time
client.connect.timeout.explanation: TCP connect to {host} did not complete within {deadline_ms} ms. Nothing was sent. Why the peer did not answer is not known from this evidence.
alternatives: A firewall silently drops the traffic.
The host is down or unreachable.
Routing or VPN configuration sends traffic elsewhere.
does_not_prove: That a firewall rule is the cause.
That the destination is permanently down.

remediation.text: Check network reachability to the host and port.

confirm_with: Try connecting from another network or host.

client.connect.unreachable.title: The network or host is unreachable
client.connect.unreachable.explanation: The operating system reported that {host} cannot be reached ({message}). Nothing was sent.
alternatives: No route to that network.
The interface or VPN is down.
does_not_prove: That the service itself is down.

remediation.text: Check network connectivity and routing on this machine.

client.connect.reset.title: The connection was reset while connecting
client.connect.reset.explanation: The TCP connection to {host} was reset during setup. Nothing was sent.
alternatives: A firewall or middlebox reset the connection.
The listener's backlog is full.
does_not_prove: Any specific cause.

remediation.text: Check listener health and middleboxes on the path.

client.connect.address_unavailable.title: No local address or port was available
client.connect.address_unavailable.explanation: This machine could not allocate a local address/port for the connection ({message}).
alternatives: Local ephemeral ports are exhausted (common during heavy load tests).
does_not_prove: Anything about the destination.

remediation.text: Reduce local connection churn (enable keep-alive) or wait for TIME_WAIT sockets to drain.

client.connect.other.title: The connection could not be established
does_not_prove: Any specific cause.

remediation.text: Check the host, port and local network.

proxy.connect_failed.title: The forward proxy could not be reached
proxy.connect_failed.explanation: Anvil could not connect to {proxy}: {message}. The destination was never contacted.
does_not_prove: That the destination API or a gateway backend is down.

remediation.text: Check the proxy address and that the proxy is running, or bypass it for this host with NO_PROXY.

proxy.auth_required.title: The proxy requires authentication
proxy.auth_required.explanation: {proxy} refused to open a tunnel without valid proxy credentials. The destination was never contacted.
does_not_prove: That the destination API rejected your API credentials.

remediation.text: Set the proxy credentials in the proxy profile.

proxy.tunnel_rejected.title: The proxy refused to connect to the destination
proxy.tunnel_rejected.explanation: {proxy} answered the tunnel request with {status}. Anvil never reached the destination, so no TLS handshake with it took place.
alternatives: The proxy's policy blocks this destination.
The proxy could not reach the destination itself.
does_not_prove: That the destination rejected TLS or the request.

remediation.text: Check the proxy's allow-list and its connectivity to the destination.

confirm_with: Proxy access logs for this tunnel.

proxy.protocol_error.title: The proxy did not complete the tunnel
does_not_prove: That the destination is at fault.

remediation.text: Confirm the proxy type (HTTP, HTTPS or SOCKS5) matches the proxy.

client.tls.verification_bypassed.title: Certificate verification is disabled for this request
client.tls.verification_bypassed.explanation: The connection to {host} was encrypted, but its certificate was not verified, so the peer's identity is not authenticated. Strict verification would have concluded that {would}.
does_not_prove: That you are talking to the intended server.

remediation.text: Trust the correct private CA in this TLS profile and turn verification back on.

client.tls.untrusted_issuer.title: The server certificate is not trusted
client.tls.untrusted_issuer.explanation: The certificate presented by {host} (issuer {issuer}) does not chain to a trusted authority in this TLS profile. This concerns the connection from Anvil to {host}, and it failed before any HTTP was exchanged.
alternatives: The server uses a private CA that this profile does not include.
The server does not send its intermediate certificates.
Something is intercepting the connection.
does_not_prove: That a gateway's connection to its backend failed.
That the server is malicious.

remediation.text: After confirming the server's identity, add the correct private CA to this workspace's TLS profile (it is never installed system-wide).
If a public certificate is expected, ask the server owner to serve the full chain.

confirm_with: Compare the presented chain's fingerprints with the expected certificate.

client.tls.expired.title: The server certificate has expired
client.tls.expired.explanation: The certificate presented by {host} expired on {not_after} according to this machine's clock. The handshake stopped before any HTTP was exchanged.
alternatives: This machine's clock is wrong.
does_not_prove: That disabling verification is appropriate.

remediation.text: Renew the server certificate.
Check this machine's date and time.

client.tls.not_yet_valid.title: The server certificate is not valid yet
client.tls.not_yet_valid.explanation: The certificate presented by {host} is valid only from {not_before} according to this machine's clock.
alternatives: This machine's clock is behind.
The certificate was issued with a future start date.
does_not_prove: That the server's clock is wrong.

remediation.text: Check this machine's date and time, then the certificate's issuance.

client.tls.name_mismatch.title: The certificate does not match the host name
client.tls.name_mismatch.explanation: The certificate from {host} is valid for {sans}, not for the name Anvil verified ({server_name}). This concerns the connection from Anvil to {host}.
alternatives: The URL uses a different name (or an IP address) than the certificate.
SNI/host routing selected a different site's certificate.
does_not_prove: That your token or credentials are invalid.

remediation.text: Use the host name the certificate was issued for, or set the TLS server name in the profile.

client.tls.revoked.title: The server certificate is revoked
client.tls.revoked.explanation: The certificate presented by {host} is marked as revoked.

remediation.text: The server owner must deploy a new certificate.

client.tls.bad_certificate.title: The server certificate is not acceptable

remediation.text: Ask the server owner to fix the certificate (encoding, key usage or signature).

client.tls.client_cert_required.title: A client certificate is required
client.tls.client_cert_required.explanation: {host} asked for a client certificate, Anvil had none selected for this destination, and the peer ended the handshake with a certificate_required alert. No HTTP response was received.
does_not_prove: That an HTTP 401 was received.
That a gateway's certificate for its backend is wrong.

remediation.text: Select the intended client certificate in the TLS profile for this host.

client.tls.client_cert_rejected.title: The peer rejected the presented client certificate
client.tls.client_cert_rejected.explanation: Anvil presented {client_subject} and {host} ended the connection with a {alert} alert. That alert is consistent with the peer not accepting this certificate.
alternatives: The peer does not trust the certificate's issuer.
The certificate is expired or not yet valid on the peer's clock.
The certificate is revoked or lacks the client-authentication usage.
The peer's policy does not allow this identity.
does_not_prove: Which of these reasons applies.
That the gateway's backend certificate is wrong.

remediation.text: Confirm with the server owner which CA and identity are accepted for this host.

confirm_with: The peer's TLS logs for this handshake.

client.tls.client_cert_probably_required.title: The handshake failed after a client certificate was requested
client.tls.client_cert_probably_required.explanation: {host} requested a client certificate, Anvil had none selected, and the peer then ended the handshake with a {alert} alert. This is consistent with a required client certificate, but the alert itself is generic.
does_not_prove: That a missing certificate was definitely the reason.

remediation.text: Select the intended client certificate for this host and retry.

confirm_with: The peer's TLS logs.

client.tls.closed_after_certificate_requ.title: The connection closed right after a client certificate was requested
client.tls.closed_after_certificate_requ.explanation: {host} asked for a client certificate during a TLS 1.3 handshake and Anvil presented {client_cert}. The new connection then closed before any response, without a TLS alert Anvil could read. In TLS 1.3 the peer checks the client certificate only after the client has finished its side of the handshake, and its refusal alert can be lost when the peer resets the connection, so this is consistent with the peer refusing the client certificate. No HTTP response was received.
alternatives: The peer closed the connection for an unrelated reason (overload, restart or connection policy).
Something between Anvil and the peer reset the connection.
does_not_prove: That the client certificate was the reason.
That an HTTP 401 was received.
That a gateway's certificate for its backend is wrong.

remediation.text: Check that the intended client certificate is selected for this host and issued by a CA the peer accepts.

confirm_with: The peer's TLS logs for this connection.

client.tls.version_mismatch.title: The peer does not support the offered TLS version
client.tls.version_mismatch.explanation: {host} ended the handshake with a protocol_version alert.

remediation.text: Check the minimum TLS version in the profile and the server's supported versions.

client.tls.peer_alert.title: The peer ended the TLS handshake
client.tls.peer_alert.explanation: {host} sent a {alert} alert. The alert shows the handshake was rejected but not why.
alternatives: Certificate policy on the server.
Cipher suite or version incompatibility.
SNI routing rejected the requested name.
does_not_prove: Any specific cause.

remediation.text: Check the server's TLS configuration and logs.

confirm_with: The server's TLS logs for this handshake.

client.tls.handshake_timeout.title: The TLS handshake did not finish in time
client.tls.handshake_timeout.explanation: TCP to {host} connected, but the TLS handshake did not complete within {deadline_ms} ms. The peer accepted the connection and then did not complete TLS.
alternatives: The service is overloaded.
The port expects a different protocol and is waiting for input.
A middlebox holds the connection.
does_not_prove: That a backend read timeout occurred.
That the server's certificate is wrong.

remediation.text: Confirm the port serves TLS and check the peer's TLS setup and load.

client.tls.connection_closed.title: The connection closed during the TLS handshake
client.tls.connection_closed.explanation: {host} closed or reset the connection during the TLS handshake without sending a TLS alert. The specific reason is unknown.
alternatives: The server requires a client certificate and drops connections without one.
SNI routing does not recognize the requested name.
The port does not speak TLS.
A middlebox reset the connection.
does_not_prove: That a client certificate is missing.
That the server certificate is invalid.

remediation.text: Check the peer's TLS logs and certificate policy.

confirm_with: The peer's logs for this connection.

client.tls.not_tls.title: The peer does not appear to speak TLS on this port
client.tls.not_tls.explanation: Anvil started TLS with {host}, but the first bytes received were not a TLS record. The port is probably serving plaintext (for example plain HTTP).
alternatives: The URL should use http:// or a different port.
does_not_prove: That a certificate expired or is invalid.

remediation.text: Check the URL scheme and port.

client.tls.alpn_mismatch.title: The required application protocol was not negotiated
alternatives: The listener does not support HTTP/2 (or the selected protocol).
does_not_prove: That authentication failed.

remediation.text: Choose a protocol the listener supports, or use automatic negotiation.

client.tls.other.title: The TLS handshake failed
does_not_prove: Any specific cause.

remediation.text: Check TLS settings on both sides.

client.quic.handshake_timeout.title: The QUIC handshake did not complete
client.quic.handshake_timeout.explanation: No QUIC handshake completed with {host} within {deadline_ms} ms. With forced HTTP/3, Anvil does not fall back to TCP.
alternatives: UDP is blocked on the path.
The server does not serve HTTP/3 on this port.
does_not_prove: That the server is down — UDP failure is not TCP failure.

remediation.text: Check UDP reachability, or choose HTTP/3 with fallback.

client.quic.idle_timeout.title: The QUIC connection went idle
client.quic.idle_timeout.explanation: The QUIC connection to {host} timed out due to inactivity.

remediation.text: Check UDP path stability.

client.quic.connection_failed.title: The QUIC connection failed
does_not_prove: That the HTTP service is down.

remediation.text: Check the HTTP/3 listener and UDP path.

client.dtls.handshake_timeout.title: The DTLS handshake did not complete
client.dtls.handshake_timeout.explanation: No DTLS handshake completed with {host} within {deadline_ms} ms. For UDP this does not show whether datagrams reached the peer.
alternatives: UDP is blocked.
The peer does not speak DTLS on this port.
The peer rejected the client identity silently.
does_not_prove: That the peer is down.

remediation.text: Check the DTLS listener, UDP reachability and the DTLS profile.
Check the DTLS certificates and trust on both sides.

client.h3.fallback_used.title: HTTP/3 was not used
client.h3.fallback_used.explanation: {from} was attempted first and failed; the response came over {to}. Each attempt is listed in the session inspector.
does_not_prove: That the server lacks HTTP/3 — the UDP path may be blocked.

remediation.text: Force HTTP/3 to test it specifically.

exchange.write_timeout.title: The request could not be sent in time
exchange.write_timeout.explanation: Anvil could not hand the full request to {host} within {deadline_ms} ms; the peer stopped reading it.
alternatives: The server is overloaded.
Flow control or a proxy is buffering the upload.
does_not_prove: That no part of the request reached the server.

remediation.text: Check server upload handling and limits.

exchange.write_failed.title: Sending the request failed
exchange.write_failed.explanation: The connection to {host} failed while the request was being written ({message}).
alternatives: The peer closed early because the request exceeded a limit.
The connection was reset by a middlebox.
does_not_prove: That the server did not see part of the request.

remediation.text: Check request size limits and the peer's logs.

exchange.headers_timeout.title: No response arrived in time
exchange.headers_timeout.explanation: The request was sent to {host}, but no response headers arrived within {deadline_ms} ms. The peer may still be working on it.
alternatives: The server (or something behind it) is slow.
The server is waiting for more request data.
does_not_prove: That the server never received the request.
That the request was not processed.

remediation.text: Increase the response-header deadline only if long processing is expected; otherwise investigate server latency.

confirm_with: Server-side logs for the request.

exchange.closed_before_response.title: The connection closed before a response
exchange.closed_before_response.explanation: {host} closed the connection after the request was sent and before sending a response. The request may or may not have been processed.
alternatives: The server crashed or restarted while handling the request.
The server closes idle/keep-alive connections at the same moment.
A middlebox dropped the connection.
does_not_prove: That the request was not processed.

remediation.text: Check whether the operation took effect before repeating it; check server logs.

confirm_with: Server logs for this request.

exchange.reset_before_response.title: The connection was reset before a response
exchange.reset_before_response.explanation: {host} reset the connection after the request was sent and before sending a response. The request may or may not have been processed.
alternatives: The server aborted the request.
A middlebox reset the connection.
The server exceeded a resource limit.
does_not_prove: That the request was not processed.

remediation.text: Check whether the operation took effect before repeating it; check server and proxy logs.

exchange.protocol_error.title: The response could not be understood
exchange.protocol_error.explanation: {host} replied with data that is not a valid response for the negotiated protocol: {message}
alternatives: The port serves a different protocol.
Cleartext HTTP/2 (h2c) was forced against an HTTP/1-only server.
does_not_prove: That a TLS handshake occurred (for cleartext connections).

remediation.text: Check the protocol setting and the port.

exchange.headers_too_large.title: The response headers are too large
exchange.headers_too_large.explanation: The response headers from {host} exceeded Anvil's header limit.

remediation.text: Raise the response header limit if this is expected.

exchange.h2_refused_stream.title: The server refused this HTTP/2 stream
exchange.h2_refused_stream.explanation: {host} refused the stream with REFUSED_STREAM. HTTP/2 guarantees that a refused stream was not processed, so repeating it is safe.

remediation.text: Retry; if it repeats, the server is limiting concurrent streams.

exchange.h2_stream_reset.title: The HTTP/2 stream was reset
exchange.h2_stream_reset.explanation: {host} reset this stream with {h2_code} before a response. Other streams on the same connection are not necessarily affected.
does_not_prove: That the whole connection or server failed.
That the request was not processed.

remediation.text: Check server logs for this stream before repeating a non-idempotent request.

exchange.h2_goaway.title: The server is closing the HTTP/2 connection
exchange.h2_goaway.explanation: {host} sent GOAWAY ({h2_code}) before this request completed.
alternatives: Graceful shutdown or restart.
The server hit a connection-level limit.
does_not_prove: That TLS failed.
Whether this request was processed.

remediation.text: Send new requests on a new connection; verify operation state before repeating.

exchange.total_timeout.title: The request exceeded its total time limit
exchange.total_timeout.explanation: The whole attempt exceeded the total deadline of {deadline_ms} ms before a response arrived.
does_not_prove: That the server did not process the request.

remediation.text: Review the total timeout for this request.

request.canceled.title: The request was canceled
request.canceled.explanation: You canceled the request before a response arrived.
does_not_prove: That the server did not receive or process the request.

request.canceled_during_body.title: Reading the response was canceled
request.canceled_during_body.explanation: Response headers with status {status} had arrived; reading the body was canceled after {bytes} bytes.

request.processing_uncertain.title: The request may have been processed
request.processing_uncertain.explanation: Request bytes left Anvil before the failure, so the server may have acted on this {method}. {replay_advice}
does_not_prove: That the operation succeeded.
That the operation did not happen.

remediation.text: Verify the operation's state (for example by reading the resource) before sending again.

confirm_with: Server-side records keyed by an idempotency key or request ID.

request.earlier_attempt_may_have_process.title: An earlier attempt may already have been processed
request.earlier_attempt_may_have_process.explanation: This {method} made {attempts} attempts. The last one was rejected before being sent, but an earlier attempt may have reached the server. The request as a whole may have taken effect.
does_not_prove: That the final rejection means nothing happened.

remediation.text: Check the operation's state before repeating it.

response.body_incomplete.title: The response body did not finish
response.body_incomplete.explanation: Response headers arrived with status {status}, but the body ended after {bytes} of {declared} bytes. This is not a complete response, even if the status indicates success.
alternatives: The server or an intermediary aborted the response.
The connection was interrupted.
does_not_prove: That the request failed on the server — it may have been processed.
That the server sent a different status.

remediation.text: Do not treat this as a successful response; check whether the operation took effect before repeating it.
Check the server's logs for aborted responses.

confirm_with: Server or gateway logs for this request.

response.body_idle_timeout.title: The response body stalled
response.body_idle_timeout.explanation: Response headers arrived with status {status}; after {bytes} body bytes, no more data arrived within {deadline_ms} ms.
alternatives: The server is slow to produce the body.
A long-lived stream was expected (use streaming/SSE mode).
does_not_prove: That the response succeeded.
That the backend's read timeout fired.

remediation.text: Check server body production; raise the body idle deadline only if long gaps are expected.

response.body_stream_reset.title: The response stream was reset
response.body_stream_reset.explanation: Response headers arrived with status {status}; the HTTP/2 stream was then reset ({h2_code}) after {bytes} body bytes. The response is incomplete.
does_not_prove: That the status reflects the final result.

remediation.text: Treat the response as failed; check server logs.

response.body_total_timeout.title: The total time limit ended the response
response.body_total_timeout.explanation: Response headers with status {status} arrived, but the body was still incomplete when the total deadline of {deadline_ms} ms elapsed.

remediation.text: Raise the total timeout for large or slow responses.

http.unauthorized.title: Authentication was refused (401)
http.unauthorized.explanation: The response status is 401: the request was missing credentials or they were not accepted.
alternatives: A gateway authentication plugin rejected the credential.
The application rejected the credential.
The credential is expired or for a different audience.
does_not_prove: Which component returned the 401.
That a TLS problem occurred.

remediation.text: Check the credential, its location (header/query) and its expiry in the Effective request.

confirm_with: The WWW-Authenticate header and a correlated gateway diagnostic.

http.forbidden.title: The request was refused (403)
http.forbidden.explanation: The service refused this request with 403. A 403 alone does not tell whether gateway authorization, a WAF/policy block or the application refused it.
alternatives: Gateway access control (ACL, IP/geo restriction, OPA).
A WAF or bot-detection policy.
The application's own authorization.
does_not_prove: That a WAF blocked the request.
That the credentials are wrong.

remediation.text: Check the credential's scope/groups and the response details.
Ask the gateway operator to correlate the request with gateway logs.

confirm_with: A correlated gateway diagnostic or log entry.

http.not_found.title: Not found (404)
alternatives: No gateway route matches this host/path.
The application has no such resource.
does_not_prove: That a gateway route is missing — applications also return 404.

remediation.text: Check the host, path and any path prefix the gateway strips or adds.

http.method_not_allowed.title: Method not allowed (405)
alternatives: The gateway route restricts methods.
The application does not implement this method.
does_not_prove: That authentication failed.
Which component rejected the method.

remediation.text: Use a documented method for this endpoint.
Configure proxy credentials.

http.request_timeout.title: Request timeout (408)
http.request_timeout.explanation: The response status is 408: the server gave up waiting for the complete request.
alternatives: The request body was sent too slowly.
A gateway's request-body read timeout fired.

remediation.text: Check upload speed and body size.

http.payload_too_large.title: The request body is too large (413)
http.payload_too_large.explanation: The response status is 413: a size limit on the path refused the request body.
alternatives: A gateway request-size limit.
The application's own limit.
does_not_prove: That the application received the full body.

remediation.text: Reduce or split the payload, or ask the owner about the intended limit.

http.unsupported_media_type.title: Unsupported media type (415)
http.unsupported_media_type.explanation: The response status is 415: the Content-Type of the request is not accepted.
alternatives: A gateway contract validator.
The application.

remediation.text: Check the Content-Type header and body encoding.

http.too_many_requests.title: Rate limited (429)
http.too_many_requests.explanation: The response status is 429: a rate or concurrency limit refused the request. {retry_after}
alternatives: A gateway rate-limiting plugin.
The application's own rate limit.
A per-IP concurrency limit.
does_not_prove: Which component applied the limit.

remediation.text: Slow down, honor Retry-After, or ask for a higher quota.

http.client_error.title: Client error ({status})
http.client_error.explanation: The response status is {status} {reason}: the request was not accepted as sent.
does_not_prove: Which component returned the status.

remediation.text: Check the request against the API's documentation.

http.bad_gateway.title: Bad gateway (502)
http.bad_gateway.explanation: The response status is 502: a proxy or gateway on the path could not get a valid response from the next hop — or an application returned 502 itself.
alternatives: A gateway could not connect to its backend.
The backend closed or reset its connection.
The application returned 502.
does_not_prove: Which hop failed.
That your connection to the gateway had a problem — it completed.

remediation.text: Ask the gateway operator to check the backend's reachability for this route.

confirm_with: Gateway logs or diagnostic detail for this request.

http.service_unavailable.title: Service unavailable (503)
http.service_unavailable.explanation: The response status is 503: a component on the path is temporarily unable to handle the request. {retry_after}
alternatives: Gateway admission control (overload, circuit breaker, stale configuration, capacity limits).
The application is overloaded or in maintenance.
does_not_prove: That CPU is exhausted.
Which component refused the request.

remediation.text: Retry later with backoff; ask the operator which limit applied.

http.gateway_timeout.title: Gateway timeout (504)
http.gateway_timeout.explanation: The response status is 504: a proxy or gateway did not get a response from the next hop in time — or an application returned 504 itself.
alternatives: The backend was slow to respond.
The backend was slow to read the upload.
The application returned 504.
does_not_prove: Which stage timed out.
That the backend never received the request.

remediation.text: Ask the operator to compare the gateway's timeouts with backend latency.

http.server_error.title: Server error ({status})
alternatives: The application failed.
A gateway or proxy generated the error.
does_not_prove: Which component produced the status.

remediation.text: Check the API's error details and server logs.

ferrum.marker.unverified.title: Ferrum-like header from an unverified destination
ferrum.marker.unverified.explanation: The response carries Ferrum diagnostic header values ({values}), but this destination is not configured as a trusted Ferrum gateway. Any server can send these headers, so Anvil does not use them to attribute the failure.
does_not_prove: That the response came from Ferrum Edge.

remediation.text: If this is your Ferrum gateway, add a trusted Ferrum integration profile for this host after verifying its identity.

ferrum.degraded_routing.title: Gateway used degraded upstream selection
ferrum.degraded_routing.explanation: The request completed with status {status}, and the gateway reported degraded upstream selection (for example, a fallback target). This is a warning about routing health, not a failed request.
does_not_prove: That this request failed.
That the gateway (not a backend or a response-header plugin) set the header — on every audited Ferrum Edge release both can add it to responses.

remediation.text: Check upstream health and target selection for this route.

ferrum.marker.conflicting.title: Conflicting gateway diagnostic values
ferrum.marker.conflicting.explanation: The response carries several different X-Gateway-Error values ({values}). Anvil does not pick one; the evidence conflicts.
alternatives: An intermediary added or duplicated the header.
A backend returned its own copy.
does_not_prove: Any one of the listed causes.

remediation.text: Inspect the raw headers and the path's intermediaries.

confirm_with: Gateway logs for this request.

ferrum.marker.unknown_token.title: Unrecognized gateway diagnostic value
ferrum.marker.unknown_token.explanation: The trusted gateway sent X-Gateway-Error: {token}, which is not in the vocabulary Anvil knows for this gateway ({basis}). Anvil shows it as-is without guessing what it means.
does_not_prove: Any interpretation based on how the value is spelled.

remediation.text: Update Anvil's compatibility catalog for this gateway version.

ferrum.marker.inconsistent.title: Gateway diagnostic value contradicts the response status
ferrum.marker.inconsistent.explanation: The response carries X-Gateway-Error: {token} on HTTP {status}. Ferrum Edge writes its diagnostic values only on 5xx responses (and gRPC trailers) ({basis}), so this value did not come from the gateway's error classification. Anvil does not use it to explain this response.
alternatives: A response-header plugin on this route added the value to a rejection.
An intermediary or the backend added the header.
does_not_prove: That the gateway applied the '{token}' outcome to this request.
Which component produced the {status} response.

remediation.text: Check the route's response-header transformation rules; X-Gateway-Error should only be written by the gateway itself.

confirm_with: Gateway logs for this request.

ferrum.token.connection_failure.title: Gateway could not prepare a connection to the backend
ferrum.token.connection_failure.explanation: Ferrum Edge reports ({token}, status {status}) that it could not set up a connection to the configured backend. This coarse value combines DNS, TCP connect, TLS, connection-pool and related setup failures; it does not say which step failed. Your own connection to the gateway completed.
alternatives: The gateway could not resolve the backend host.
The backend refused or did not accept the connection.
The gateway's TLS connection to the backend failed.
A gateway connection-pool or connection-limit problem.
does_not_prove: That TLS failed.
That DNS failed.
That your client certificate is wrong — the gateway's connection to its backend uses the gateway's identity.

remediation.text: Check the backend host and port, the gateway's DNS/network access to it, and the gateway's backend TLS settings.

confirm_with: Gateway logs or authorized diagnostic detail for this request.

ferrum.token.backend_timeout.title: Gateway reported a backend timeout
ferrum.token.backend_timeout.explanation: Ferrum Edge reports ({token}, status {status}) a timeout while exchanging with the backend. The value does not say which stage (upload, waiting for headers, body) timed out. {release_detail}
alternatives: The backend was slow to produce response headers.
The backend stopped reading the upload.
The backend's body stalled.
The backend itself returned 504.
does_not_prove: Which stage timed out.
That the backend never received the request.
That the backend received the request.

remediation.text: Compare the route's timeouts with backend latency; check backend logs.

ferrum.token.backend_error.title: Gateway classified this as a backend error
ferrum.token.backend_error.explanation: Ferrum Edge marked this response with {token} (status {status}). The value covers 5xx responses the backend returned itself as well as failures and refusals on the gateway side, and it does not say which of these happened. {release_detail}
alternatives: The application returned this 5xx itself.
The backend reset or closed the connection.
A gateway-local limit was reached (retained-buffer capacity or in-flight request limit).
A gateway response policy (for example an AI response guard or a response validator) rejected a response the backend had delivered.
Gateway egress policy refused the backend address.
does_not_prove: That the application itself produced this error.
That the gateway's connection to the backend failed.
That the backend is unhealthy.

remediation.text: Check the response body and the backend's logs for this request.
Correlate with gateway logs to separate gateway-observed failures from application responses.

ferrum.token.circuit_breaker_open.title: Gateway circuit breaker rejected this attempt
ferrum.token.circuit_breaker_open.explanation: Ferrum Edge rejected this attempt ({token}, status {status}) because the circuit breaker for the upstream is open after recent failures.
does_not_prove: That no earlier attempt of this request reached a backend.

remediation.text: Check upstream health; the breaker closes after its recovery period.

ferrum.token.overload.title: Gateway refused the request (overload category)
ferrum.token.overload.explanation: Ferrum Edge refused this request with {token} (status {status}). This value covers gateway overload and draining refusals, and also the response-transformer output size ceiling.
alternatives: The gateway is at its admission limit.
The gateway is draining.
A response transformation exceeded the output size ceiling.
does_not_prove: That CPU is exhausted.
That the application is overloaded.

remediation.text: Reduce offered load or retry later; the operator can check gateway resources, drain state and transform limits.

ferrum.token.config_stale.title: Gateway configuration is stale
ferrum.token.config_stale.explanation: Ferrum Edge refused this request ({token}, status {status}) because its data plane has not received fresh configuration within the allowed window.
does_not_prove: That anything in your request is wrong — changing the payload will not help.

remediation.text: Restore control-plane connectivity or configuration freshness.

ferrum.token.concurrency_limit.title: Gateway adaptive concurrency limit
ferrum.token.concurrency_limit.explanation: Ferrum Edge refused this request ({token}, status {status}) at its adaptive concurrency admission control for the upstream.
does_not_prove: That the backend crashed.
That an API rate limit was hit.

remediation.text: Reduce concurrency; the operator can review latency signals and admission settings.

ferrum.marker.absent.title: No gateway diagnostic marker on this error
ferrum.marker.absent.explanation: This {status} came through the trusted gateway profile without an X-Gateway-Error value. The absence of a marker does not identify where the error originated. {release_detail}
alternatives: A gateway plugin rejected the request (for example an authorization dependency failing closed); plugin rejections need not carry an X-Gateway-Error value.
The application returned the error and the gateway did not classify it.
An intermediary removed the header.
The error came from a component outside the gateway.
does_not_prove: That the upstream application produced the error.

remediation.text: Correlate with gateway logs.

ferrum.outcome.title: Matches a known gateway outcome
alternatives: A backend returned a response with identical status and body.
confirm_with: Gateway logs or authorized diagnostic detail for this request.

ferrum.outcome_ambiguous.title: Several known causes produce this exact response
ferrum.outcome_ambiguous.explanation: This response matches {count} different Ferrum Edge outcomes that look identical from the client. The common, safe conclusion: {common}
alternatives: A backend returned a response with identical status and body.
does_not_prove: Which of the listed causes applied.
That the gateway (rather than a backend returning identical bytes) authored this response.

remediation.text: Ask the gateway operator for the correlated log entry or diagnostic detail to tell these apart.

ferrum.backend_passthrough.title: The backend's own response passed through the gateway
ferrum.backend_passthrough.explanation: The body is not a gateway-generated error body. On {release}, a backend's own {status} passes through with the gateway marker {token}. This is consistent with the application producing the status.
alternatives: An intermediary behind the gateway produced it.
does_not_prove: That the gateway produced the error.

remediation.text: Check the application's logs and the error body.

ferrum.relayed_backend_response.title: The gateway relayed this response from behind it
ferrum.relayed_backend_response.explanation: The body matches a gateway rejection ({outcome}), but the {status} response carries the gateway's own Via hop ({via}). {release} adds that hop only to responses built on its backend path; its authentication and authorization rejections never carry it. This response most likely came from the service behind the gateway, not from the gateway's own checks.
alternatives: Another gateway or proxy behind this one produced the rejection.
The application reuses the gateway's error wording.
does_not_prove: Which component behind the gateway produced it.
That the gateway authored the body, even though the text matches.

remediation.text: Check the application's (or the next hop's) authentication and authorization logs for this request.

confirm_with: The gateway's transaction log for this request, which shows whether the backend was called.

app.soap_fault.title: The SOAP service returned a fault
app.soap_fault.explanation: The transport succeeded (status {status}), but the SOAP body is a Fault: {fault_code} — {fault_reason}.
does_not_prove: That the HTTP status indicates success at the application level.

remediation.text: Read the fault code and fix the request or ask the service owner.

app.graphql_errors.title: The GraphQL response contains errors
app.graphql_errors.explanation: The transport succeeded (status {status}), but the response lists {count} GraphQL error(s), starting with: {first}. {partial}
does_not_prove: That HTTP 200 means the operation fully succeeded.

remediation.text: Inspect each error's path; partial data may still be usable.

app.grpc_status.title: The RPC failed: {name}
app.grpc_status.explanation: The call ended with grpc-status {code} ({name}) {message}. HTTP status was {http_status}; for gRPC, HTTP 200 does not mean the RPC succeeded. {trailers_only}
does_not_prove: Which component (gateway or service) produced the status, when it came as a trailers-only response.

remediation.text: Handle the status per the service's contract; check grpc-status-details if present.

app.grpc_status_missing.title: The RPC ended without a status
app.grpc_status_missing.explanation: HTTP status {http_status} arrived, but the stream ended without a grpc-status. The RPC result is unknown — it is not a success.
alternatives: The server or an intermediary aborted the stream.
A deadline or connection problem cut the stream.
does_not_prove: That the RPC succeeded or failed on the server.

remediation.text: Check server logs and stream completion before repeating non-idempotent calls.

grpc.framing_invalid.title: The {wire} response framing is invalid
grpc.framing_invalid.explanation: HTTP status {http_status} arrived and the response body could be read, but it is not valid {wire} framing: {problem}. {status_note}
alternatives: The server wrote a malformed body.
An intermediary changed the body, for example by appending or re-framing gRPC-Web frames, or passed the request to a server that answers in a different framing.
does_not_prove: Which hop produced the malformed bytes.
Whether the RPC took effect on the server.

remediation.text: Capture the raw response at each hop (client, gateway, server) to find where the framing changes.

confirm_with: The server's and any proxy's logs for this call.

grpc_web.no_trailer_frame.title: The gRPC-Web response had no trailer frame
grpc_web.no_trailer_frame.explanation: HTTP status {http_status} arrived with content type {content_type}, and the response body ended cleanly without the trailer frame (flag 0x80) that carries grpc-status in gRPC-Web. {status_note}
alternatives: The server, or a proxy in front of it, answered with native gRPC framing, whose status travels in HTTP trailers.
A hop passed the gRPC-Web request through to a server that does not speak gRPC-Web.
The server ended the response before writing its status.
does_not_prove: Which hop dropped the trailer frame or never produced it.
Whether any gateway on the path translates gRPC-Web, or is configured to.
That the RPC succeeded or failed on the server.

remediation.text: Check that the server, or the proxy in front of it, speaks gRPC-Web for this route; native gRPC over HTTP/2 or HTTP/3 reads the status from HTTP trailers instead.

confirm_with: The server's or proxy's logs for this call, and whether the route is expected to serve gRPC-Web.

ws.handshake_rejected.title: The WebSocket handshake was rejected
ws.handshake_rejected.explanation: The server answered the upgrade with HTTP {status} instead of switching protocols.
alternatives: Authentication or origin policy refused the upgrade.
The endpoint does not support WebSocket over this bootstrap.

remediation.text: Check the response body, credentials, Origin and the selected bootstrap (HTTP/1.1 Upgrade vs extended CONNECT).

ws.closed_normally.title: The WebSocket session ended normally
ws.closed_normally.explanation: {closer} closed the session with code {code} {reason}. This is a normal end, not a network error.

ws.closed_abnormally.title: The WebSocket connection ended abnormally
ws.closed_abnormally.explanation: The connection ended without a WebSocket Close frame (reported as 1006). Code 1006 is never sent by a peer; it means the connection dropped.
alternatives: The server process or an intermediary dropped the connection.
A network interruption.
does_not_prove: That the peer chose to close the session.

remediation.text: Check server and proxy logs around this time.

ws.closed_policy.title: The WebSocket was closed for policy reasons (1008)
alternatives: A gateway security policy (e.g. WAF message inspection).
The application's own policy.
does_not_prove: Which component applied the policy.

remediation.text: Review the message content that triggered the close.

ws.closed_too_big.title: A WebSocket message was too large (1009)
ws.closed_too_big.explanation: The session was closed with 1009 {reason}: a message exceeded a size limit.
alternatives: The peer's limit.
Anvil's local message limit.
does_not_prove: That the message was corrupt.

remediation.text: Send smaller messages or adjust the limit intentionally.

ws.closed_other.title: The WebSocket was closed by the peer ({code})
ws.closed_other.explanation: The peer closed the session with code {code} {reason}.
alternatives: The application closed the session with this code.
A gateway or proxy on the path closed the session itself, for example because its own upstream connection ended without a Close frame.
does_not_prove: Which hop authored the Close frame: the peer Anvil is connected to may be a proxy speaking for its upstream.

remediation.text: Check the application's and any gateway's logs for this session.

confirm_with: Gateway or proxy logs for this WebSocket session.

sse.canceled.title: The event stream was stopped
sse.canceled.explanation: The event stream was stopped after {events} events, as requested. This is an expected end, not a server timeout.

sse.idle_timeout.title: The event stream went quiet
sse.idle_timeout.explanation: No event arrived within the idle limit after {events} events.
alternatives: The server has no new events.
The connection stalled.
does_not_prove: That the server failed.

remediation.text: Raise the idle limit if long gaps between events are normal.

dtls.closed_without_response.title: The DTLS peer closed the session without answering
dtls.closed_without_response.explanation: The DTLS handshake with {host} completed from Anvil's side, {sent} datagram(s) were sent, and the peer then closed the session (close_notify) without sending any data back.
alternatives: The peer did not accept the client certificate. With DTLS 1.3 the peer checks it only after the client's final handshake flight, so the client sees the handshake finish before the refusal.
A gateway in front of the service could not set up its own connection to the backend and closed the session.
The peer's policy ended the session.
does_not_prove: Which of these reasons applies.
That the datagrams reached an application.
That nothing is listening on the port: a DTLS peer answered the handshake.

remediation.text: Check the client identity selected in the DTLS profile against the peer's accepted CA.
Check the peer's (or gateway's) logs for this session's close reason.

confirm_with: The peer's or gateway's logs for this session.

udp.no_response.title: No UDP response was observed
udp.no_response.explanation: {sent} datagram(s) were sent and none were received within {window_ms} ms. UDP gives no delivery confirmation: silence shows only that no response was observed.
alternatives: The peer received the data but does not reply.
The datagrams were lost or filtered.
Nothing is listening on the port.
does_not_prove: That the datagrams were delivered.
That the peer or a gateway is down.

remediation.text: Check what the protocol expects, and whether UDP is allowed on the path.

confirm_with: A packet capture or the peer's logs.

udp.partial_responses.title: Fewer UDP responses than datagrams sent
udp.partial_responses.explanation: {sent} datagram(s) sent, {received} received within {window_ms} ms. Sent is not delivered: UDP does not acknowledge datagrams.
alternatives: Packet loss.
The peer answers only some messages.
does_not_prove: Which datagrams were lost.

tcp.reply_after_half_close.title: The peer replied after Anvil finished sending
tcp.reply_after_half_close.explanation: Anvil half-closed its side after sending; the peer still returned {bytes} bytes. The reply was preserved.

tcp.closed_without_data.title: The connection closed without any data
tcp.closed_without_data.explanation: The TCP connection to {host} was established and {sent} byte(s) were sent, but the peer {how} before sending anything back. A layer-4 proxy (such as a gateway stream listener) has no way to say why it closed; the cause is recorded only on the peer or proxy.
alternatives: A proxy or gateway on the path could not reach, or was refused by, its own upstream.
The peer's TLS, policy or rate-limit checks rejected the connection after accepting it.
The service accepts connections but closes them for this input.
does_not_prove: That the connection from Anvil failed: its TCP (and any TLS) setup completed.
That the destination service is down.
Whether the bytes that were sent were processed.

remediation.text: Check the peer's or the proxy/gateway operator's logs for this connection; a layer-4 proxy records the cause only there.

confirm_with: Operator logs for the stream listener at this time (for example the gateway's error class and disconnect cause).

tcp.closed_abnormally.title: The TCP session ended abnormally
tcp.closed_abnormally.explanation: The connection to {host} was reset or ended with an error after {bytes} byte(s) had been received.
alternatives: The peer aborted the connection.
A proxy or gateway on the path tore the relay down (for example because its own upstream failed or an idle limit expired).
A network interruption.
does_not_prove: Which hop ended the connection.
That the destination service is down.

remediation.text: Check the peer's (or the proxy/gateway operator's) logs for this connection.

confirm_with: Operator logs of the peer or the stream proxy at this time.

auth.browser_session_required.title: This destination expects an interactive browser login
auth.browser_session_required.explanation: {host} {how}. The request stopped at a login step and did not reach the API. A login completed in a system browser creates a session cookie that stays in that browser: Anvil does not read or import browser cookies, so a browser that shows the page as signed in does not make Anvil's requests authenticated.
alternatives: The route also accepts an API credential (for example a bearer token) that this request did not present.
The session cookie that was sent has expired or was not accepted.
does_not_prove: That the credentials you use in the browser are wrong.
That Anvil's request was authenticated, even if a following page answered 200.
Which component (gateway or application) runs the login.

remediation.text: Use an API credential the service accepts for programmatic access (for example an access token from the identity provider).
If you are authorized to reuse a browser session, copy that session cookie explicitly into this request or its workspace as a secret; Anvil never takes it from the browser by itself.

confirm_with: The route's authentication settings (which credentials it accepts besides a browser session).

auth.token_expired_locally.title: The token appears to be expired
auth.token_expired_locally.explanation: The bearer token's exp claim ({when}) is in the past by this machine's clock. The token was decoded, not verified; the request was still sent so the server's own verdict is visible.
alternatives: This machine's clock is ahead.
does_not_prove: That the server rejected the token for this reason.
That the token's signature is valid.

remediation.text: Obtain a current token from its issuer.

confirm_with: The server's authentication error details.

auth.token_not_yet_valid_locally.title: The token is not valid yet
auth.token_not_yet_valid_locally.explanation: The bearer token's nbf claim ({when}) is in the future by this machine's clock. The token was decoded, not verified.
alternatives: This machine's clock is behind.
The issuer's clock is ahead.
does_not_prove: That the gateway's clock is wrong.

remediation.text: Check clocks on this machine and the issuer; wait until the token becomes valid.

masque.proxy_refused.title: The MASQUE proxy refused the UDP tunnel
masque.proxy_refused.explanation: The proxy {proxy} answered the CONNECT-UDP request for {target} with HTTP {status}. No tunnel was opened and no datagram was sent. The refusal is the proxy's answer; the status alone does not say whether the proxy ever tried to reach {target}.
alternatives: The proxy's policy does not allow this destination (for example a 403 for a target that is not configured on the route).
CONNECT-UDP is disabled on the proxy, or this route does not allow CONNECT (501, 405 or 404).
The request was malformed for the proxy, such as a URI Template the proxy does not accept (400).
The proxy could not resolve or reach the destination on its side (502 or 504, often with a Proxy-Status header).
does_not_prove: That {target} is down, unreachable or not listening — the refusal came from the proxy, and no datagram reached the target through this tunnel.
Which component behind the proxy's address wrote the answer, unless the proxy is configured as a trusted gateway.

remediation.text: Read the response body and any Proxy-Status header, then check the URI Template, the target host and port, and the credentials sent on the CONNECT request.
Check that the proxy enables CONNECT-UDP for this route and allows this destination.

confirm_with: The proxy's access log for this CONNECT-UDP request.

masque.extended_connect_unavailable.title: The proxy does not offer extended CONNECT over HTTP/3
masque.extended_connect_unavailable.explanation: The HTTP/3 SETTINGS of {proxy} do not enable extended CONNECT (SETTINGS_ENABLE_CONNECT_PROTOCOL), which RFC 9298 CONNECT-UDP requires. Anvil sent no request and no datagram to {target}.
alternatives: The proxy supports neither WebSocket over HTTP/3 nor CONNECT-UDP on this listener.
The address is an ordinary HTTP/3 server rather than a MASQUE proxy.
does_not_prove: Anything about {target} — nothing was sent toward it.
That the proxy would refuse CONNECT-UDP over another protocol version; only this HTTP/3 connection was examined.

remediation.text: Check the proxy address and port, or enable CONNECT-UDP (extended CONNECT) on the proxy's HTTP/3 listener.

confirm_with: The proxy's HTTP/3 configuration for extended CONNECT.

masque.settings_not_received.title: The proxy's HTTP/3 settings did not arrive
masque.settings_not_received.explanation: The QUIC connection to {proxy} was established, but its HTTP/3 SETTINGS frame did not arrive in time, so it is unknown whether the proxy allows extended CONNECT. Anvil sent no CONNECT-UDP request and no datagram to {target}.
alternatives: The proxy is slow to open its HTTP/3 control stream.
Packets from the proxy are being lost after the handshake.
does_not_prove: That the proxy does not support CONNECT-UDP.
Anything about {target} — nothing was sent toward it.

remediation.text: Retry, or raise the response-header timeout if the path is slow.

confirm_with: A packet capture of the QUIC connection to the proxy.

masque.no_datagram_support.title: The proxy does not offer HTTP/3 datagrams
masque.no_datagram_support.explanation: This request required UDP payloads in QUIC DATAGRAM frames, but {proxy} did not offer them: its HTTP/3 SETTINGS do not enable SETTINGS_H3_DATAGRAM, or QUIC did not negotiate DATAGRAM frames. Anvil sent no request and no datagram to {target}.
alternatives: The proxy carries HTTP Datagrams as DATAGRAM capsules on the CONNECT stream only (RFC 9297 §3.5), which the automatic mode uses.
does_not_prove: That the proxy cannot relay UDP — it may do so with capsules.
Anything about {target} — nothing was sent toward it.

remediation.text: Use the automatic or capsule datagram mode for this proxy.
Enable HTTP/3 datagrams on the proxy if QUIC DATAGRAM frames are required.

masque.tunnel_ended_abnormally.title: The UDP tunnel ended abnormally
masque.tunnel_ended_abnormally.explanation: The proxy {proxy} opened the CONNECT-UDP tunnel to {target}, but the tunnel then ended without a clean close: the proxy reset the CONNECT stream, the QUIC connection was lost, or the stream ended in the middle of a capsule. Datagrams exchanged before the end are kept; the exchange is incomplete.
alternatives: The proxy ended the tunnel (idle limit, policy or configuration change, drain, or an authorization lifetime).
The proxy's UDP socket toward the target failed.
The network path to the proxy failed.
does_not_prove: That {target} stopped responding or is down.
Which datagrams, if any, reached {target}.

remediation.text: Check the proxy's log for why this tunnel ended.

confirm_with: The proxy's log entry for this tunnel.

client.tls.spiffe_id_mismatch.title: The server's SPIFFE ID is not the expected one
client.tls.spiffe_id_mismatch.explanation: {host} presented a valid X.509-SVID that chains to this profile's trust bundle, but its SPIFFE ID is {peer_spiffe_id}, not {expected}. Anvil verifies this server by SPIFFE identity (not by host name), so it ended the handshake before any request was sent.
alternatives: The request reached a different workload than intended (routing, SNI or an address that now belongs to another workload).
The expected SPIFFE ID in the TLS profile is outdated (the workload's service account or namespace changed).
does_not_prove: That the server's certificate is untrusted: its chain was valid for the configured trust domain.
That the server received or rejected the request: nothing was sent.

remediation.text: Check which workload should answer on this address and update the expected SPIFFE ID in the TLS profile only if the presented identity is the intended one.

confirm_with: The destination workload's SVID (its SPIFFE ID) from the mesh control plane or the workload itself.

client.tls.untrusted_trust_domain.title: The server's SPIFFE trust domain is not trusted
client.tls.untrusted_trust_domain.explanation: {host} presented an identity outside the trusted trust domain {trust_domain}: {detail}. Anvil verifies this server by SPIFFE identity and ended the handshake before any request was sent.
alternatives: The server belongs to another mesh or trust domain (for example a federated cluster) whose trust bundle this profile does not include.
The TLS profile names the wrong trust domain.
does_not_prove: That the server's own certificate is malformed.
That the server received the request: nothing was sent.

remediation.text: Trust only the intended trust domain: set the profile's trust domain and add that domain's trust bundle (CA certificates), never an unrelated one.

confirm_with: The trust domains the mesh federates and their bundles.

client.tls.invalid_svid.title: The server certificate is not a valid X.509-SVID
client.tls.invalid_svid.explanation: The TLS profile verifies {host} by SPIFFE identity, but its certificate is not a valid X.509-SVID: {detail}. Anvil ended the handshake before any request was sent.
alternatives: The server is not a SPIFFE workload (an ordinary TLS server answered on this address).
The server's SVID was issued with several URI SANs or a malformed SPIFFE ID.
does_not_prove: That the certificate chain is untrusted: this concerns the identity it carries.
That the server received the request: nothing was sent.

remediation.text: Point the request at the mesh listener that serves an X.509-SVID, or remove the SPIFFE check from the TLS profile for a non-mesh server.
If this is the intended mesh workload, reissue its SVID with exactly one spiffe:// URI SAN.

client.tls.sni_override.title: A configured TLS server name was used
client.tls.sni_override.explanation: For {host}, Anvil {sni_sent} from the TLS profile's server-name override ({server_name}) instead of the URL host, and verified the server by {identity_check}. The HTTP authority is unchanged.
does_not_prove: That the override name reached the intended virtual host or passthrough route; only the handshake outcome shows that.

remediation.text: Remove the override when it is no longer needed; mesh east-west passthrough names (outbound_.PORT_._.HOST) only make sense for a gateway that routes on SNI.

hbone.endpoint_unreachable.title: The HBONE endpoint could not be reached
hbone.endpoint_unreachable.explanation: Anvil could not connect to the HBONE endpoint {endpoint}: {detail}. No tunnel was opened, so {authority} was never contacted.
alternatives: The endpoint address or port in the proxy profile is wrong.
The mesh listener (for example the HBONE or inbound port) is not running or is bound elsewhere.
does_not_prove: That the destination {authority} is down: it was never contacted.

remediation.text: Check the HBONE endpoint address in the proxy profile and that the mesh listener is up.

hbone.endpoint_identity_rejected.title: Anvil rejected the HBONE endpoint's identity
hbone.endpoint_identity_rejected.explanation: Anvil verified the HBONE endpoint {endpoint} by {expected} and rejected it: {problem}. The endpoint's certificate names {peer_spiffe_id}. This decision was made by Anvil on the client leg; no tunnel was opened and {authority} was never contacted.
alternatives: The endpoint address belongs to a different mesh proxy or workload than intended.
The proxy's TLS profile has the wrong trust bundle, trust domain or expected SPIFFE ID.
does_not_prove: That the endpoint rejected Anvil's client SVID: the handshake stopped on Anvil's side.
Anything about the destination {authority}.

remediation.text: Confirm which mesh proxy should terminate this tunnel, then correct the trust bundle or expected identity in the HBONE proxy's TLS profile.

confirm_with: The endpoint's SVID as issued by the mesh (SPIFFE ID and trust bundle).

hbone.client_svid_required.title: The HBONE endpoint requires a client SVID
hbone.client_svid_required.explanation: The HBONE endpoint {endpoint} asked for a client certificate, Anvil presented none, and the endpoint ended the handshake with a {alert} alert. HBONE is mutual TLS: without a client SVID no tunnel is opened, and {authority} was never contacted.
does_not_prove: That the destination {authority} or its policy refused anything: the tunnel was never opened.

remediation.text: Add the workload's client SVID (certificate chain and key) to the HBONE proxy's TLS profile, and check that its host bindings include the endpoint.

hbone.client_svid_rejected.title: The HBONE endpoint rejected the client SVID
hbone.client_svid_rejected.explanation: Anvil presented {client_svid} and the HBONE endpoint {endpoint} ended the mutual-TLS handshake with a {alert} alert. That alert is consistent with the endpoint not accepting this SVID. No tunnel was opened and {authority} was never contacted.
alternatives: The SVID's trust domain is not trusted (or federated) by the endpoint.
The SVID chains to a CA the endpoint does not trust, or it is expired, revoked or lacks the client-authentication usage.
does_not_prove: Which of these reasons applies: the alert does not say.
That a mesh authorization policy denied the request: admission did not get that far.

remediation.text: Use an SVID issued by the mesh's trust domain (or a federated one the endpoint trusts).

confirm_with: The endpoint's TLS/handshake logs for this connection.

hbone.endpoint_tls_failed.title: Mutual TLS with the HBONE endpoint failed
hbone.endpoint_tls_failed.explanation: The mutual-TLS handshake with the HBONE endpoint {endpoint} failed: {detail}. No tunnel was opened and {authority} was never contacted.
alternatives: The endpoint is not speaking TLS on this port.
A timeout or connection reset interrupted the handshake.
does_not_prove: Which side ended the handshake or why, beyond the recorded failure.
Anything about the destination {authority}.

remediation.text: Check that the proxy profile points at the mesh's mTLS listener (HBONE or inbound port).

hbone.tunnel_refused.title: The HBONE endpoint refused to open the tunnel
hbone.tunnel_refused.explanation: The HBONE endpoint {endpoint} answered the HTTP/2 CONNECT to {authority} with HTTP {status}. Its body says {body_error}. The tunnel was not opened: {authority} was never contacted and nothing was sent to it.
alternatives: A mesh authorization policy denied this client identity.
The endpoint only relays to destinations it terminates for, and {authority} is not one of them.
The endpoint has no route or relay for {authority} (some mesh terminators answer 404 for a destination they do not terminate).
The endpoint did not accept the client as an authenticated mesh peer (for example no or an untrusted client SVID).
does_not_prove: Which mesh policy or admission rule refused the tunnel: the public response does not identify it beyond its body, and several reasons can share one response.
That the destination {authority} is down or refused anything.

remediation.text: Check the tunnel's CONNECT authority and the client SVID used, then ask the mesh operator which policy applies to this identity and destination.

confirm_with: The mesh proxy's operator log or policy-deny records for this CONNECT.

hbone.tunnel_unavailable.title: The HBONE endpoint could not open the tunnel
hbone.tunnel_unavailable.explanation: The HBONE endpoint {endpoint} answered the HTTP/2 CONNECT to {authority} with HTTP {status}. Its body says {body_error}. No tunnel was opened and nothing was sent to {authority}.
alternatives: The endpoint could not reach or dial the destination.
The endpoint is overloaded or at a session limit.
does_not_prove: Which of these applies, or whether the destination itself is down: a 5xx on CONNECT does not say which leg failed.

remediation.text: Retry later; if it persists, ask the mesh operator to check the endpoint's view of the destination.

confirm_with: The mesh proxy's operator log for this CONNECT.

hbone.tunnel_protocol_error.title: The HBONE tunnel could not be set up over HTTP/2
hbone.tunnel_protocol_error.explanation: The HTTP/2 exchange with the HBONE endpoint {endpoint} failed before a CONNECT answer: {detail}. No tunnel was opened and {authority} was never contacted.
alternatives: The endpoint does not speak HTTP/2 (HBONE requires ALPN h2).
The endpoint reset the stream or closed the connection.
The configured connect deadline elapsed.
does_not_prove: That the destination {authority} refused anything: it was never contacted.

remediation.text: Check that the proxy profile points at an HBONE (HTTP/2 CONNECT) listener.

hbone.closed_after_certificate_request.title: The HBONE endpoint closed the connection after asking for a client certificate
hbone.closed_after_certificate_request.explanation: The HBONE endpoint {endpoint} requested a client certificate during the TLS 1.3 handshake; Anvil presented {client_svid}, completed its side of the handshake, and the fresh connection then closed before any answer to the CONNECT ({detail}). No TLS alert was readable, which is how a TLS 1.3 server's rejection of a missing or unacceptable client certificate often looks when its reset discards the alert. The tunnel was not opened and {authority} was never contacted.
alternatives: The endpoint required a client SVID and none was presented, or it did not accept the presented one.
The endpoint closed the connection for an unrelated reason (overload, restart).
does_not_prove: Which of these applies: no alert or HTTP/2 answer was received.
Anything about the destination {authority}.

remediation.text: Check that the HBONE proxy's TLS profile carries the workload's client SVID from the mesh's trust domain and that its host bindings include the endpoint.

confirm_with: The endpoint's operator log for this handshake (for example 'peer sent no certificates').

hbone.udp_tunnel_ended.title: The UDP tunnel through the HBONE endpoint ended early
hbone.udp_tunnel_ended.explanation: The datagram tunnel to {authority} through the HBONE endpoint {endpoint} ended before Anvil closed it: {how}. {received} datagram(s) had been received and {sent} sent; they are kept. No datagram can travel on this tunnel any more.
alternatives: The endpoint's UDP socket toward {authority} failed, for example after an ICMP port-unreachable (a Ferrum Mesh relay ends the tunnel when that socket reports an error).
The endpoint's idle limit for the datagram relay elapsed.
The endpoint withdrew the tunnel's admission (a trust or policy change) or is shutting down.
The network path to the endpoint failed (only when the connection was lost without an HTTP/2 frame).
does_not_prove: That {authority} is down, or which datagrams reached it: UDP gives no delivery confirmation.
Which of these ended the tunnel: the endpoint sends no reason with END_STREAM or a reset.

remediation.text: Check the mesh proxy's log for the relay of this tunnel (how and when it ended, and its byte counts).

confirm_with: The mesh proxy's operator log for this CONNECT and its relay.

hbone.udp_record_truncated.title: The UDP tunnel ended inside a datagram record
hbone.udp_record_truncated.explanation: The HBONE endpoint {endpoint} ended the datagram tunnel to {authority} in the middle of a [u16 length][payload] record: {bytes} byte(s) of an incomplete record were discarded and are not counted as a datagram. The {received} complete datagram(s) before it were received intact. The exchange is incomplete.
alternatives: The endpoint stopped its relay while it was writing a datagram (a shutdown or an error mid-write).
The endpoint does not frame this stream as Ferrum Mesh datagram records (it is not a datagram relay for this CONNECT).
does_not_prove: What the incomplete datagram contained, or whether {authority} sent it complete.
That {authority} is at fault: the framing is written by the endpoint.

remediation.text: Check the mesh proxy's log for this tunnel; if the endpoint is not a Ferrum Mesh datagram relay, send UDP to it without the HBONE proxy.

confirm_with: The mesh proxy's operator log for this CONNECT and its relay.

hbone.udp_datagram_too_large.title: A datagram was too large for an HBONE UDP record
hbone.udp_datagram_too_large.explanation: {count} datagram(s) longer than {limit} bytes were refused by Anvil and not sent: one HBONE datagram record carries at most {limit} bytes (a u16 length prefix). The other datagrams of the session were sent as usual.
does_not_prove: Anything about the endpoint {endpoint} or the destination {authority}: this was a local decision before sending.

remediation.text: Send datagrams of at most 65,535 bytes (IPv4 UDP itself carries at most 65,507, and many paths far less).

tcp.proxy_header_maybe_rejected.title: The PROXY protocol header may have been rejected
tcp.proxy_header_maybe_rejected.explanation: Anvil wrote a {format} header ({length} bytes) at the head of the connection to {host}, and the peer then {how} without sending any data. A listener that requires PROXY protocol closes the connection this way when the header is malformed or arrives from a peer it does not trust, but the same close also happens for causes unrelated to the header. {malformed}
alternatives: The address Anvil connected from is not a trusted proxy for this listener (for Ferrum Edge: not inside FERRUM_TRUSTED_PROXIES), so the listener closed before reading the header.
The listener does not accept this header version or form.
The header was accepted, and a proxy or gateway on the path then could not reach, or was refused by, its own upstream.
The listener does not expect a PROXY header and treated it as application data it could not use.
does_not_prove: That the header was rejected: a layer-4 listener sends no reason when it closes.
Which check failed (the source trust, the header format, or something after the header).
That the connection from Anvil failed: its TCP setup completed and the header was written.

remediation.text: Compare the header recorded in the connection evidence with the listener's PROXY protocol settings, and check that the address Anvil connects from is a trusted proxy for the listener.
Check the listener's logs for this connection; a Ferrum Edge stream listener logs a warning that names an untrusted peer or an invalid PROXY header.
