confirm_with: Operator logs for the listener at this time (a Ferrum Edge stream listener: "socket peer is not in FERRUM_TRUSTED_PROXIES" or "did not start with a valid PROXY header").

ferrum.catalog.unavailable.title: No audited catalog for this gateway version
ferrum.catalog.unavailable.explanation: The trusted Ferrum profile {profile} declares compatibility {compat}, but Anvil has no source-audited outcome catalog for that version (catalogs available: {available}). Anvil therefore does not compare this response with known gateway outcomes, and reads any X-Gateway-Error value only with the coarse meaning every audited release shares.
alternatives: The gateway behaves like an audited release for this response.
The gateway release changed a status, body or marker that Anvil's audited catalogs describe differently.
does_not_prove: Which gateway outcome produced this response.
That this gateway release uses the same response bodies or markers as an audited release.

remediation.text: Set the profile's compatibility version to the release this gateway actually runs, if Anvil has a catalog for it; otherwise use an Anvil build that supports that release.

confirm_with: The gateway's release version from its operator (for example `ferrum-edge --version`).

ws.deflate_not_negotiated.title: permessage-deflate was offered but not negotiated
ws.deflate_not_negotiated.explanation: Anvil offered {offered}, but the handshake answer named {answered}, so the session ran uncompressed. This is not an error: a server may decline any extension, and an intermediary may remove the offer or the answer.
alternatives: The server does not support permessage-deflate, or chose not to use it for this session.
A proxy or gateway between Anvil and the server removed the Sec-WebSocket-Extensions offer or answer; some gateways never negotiate WebSocket extensions.
does_not_prove: That the server cannot compress.
Which hop dropped the offer: the server, or a proxy or gateway in front of it.

remediation.text: Nothing is required. To see which hop drops the offer, send the same request directly to the backend and compare the answers.

confirm_with: The server's handshake log, and the same request sent without any intermediary.

ws.extension_answer_refused.title: The server's WebSocket extension answer was refused
ws.extension_answer_refused.explanation: The handshake answer's Sec-WebSocket-Extensions ({answered}) does not fit what Anvil offered ({offered}): {problem}. RFC 6455 §4.1 and RFC 7692 §7 require the client to fail the connection, so no message was exchanged.
alternatives: The server's extension negotiation is incorrect for this offer.
An intermediary added or rewrote the Sec-WebSocket-Extensions answer.
does_not_prove: That the WebSocket endpoint works incorrectly otherwise.
Which hop wrote the answer: the server, or a proxy or gateway in front of it.

remediation.text: Make the server answer only with extensions that were offered, with valid parameters that fit the offer.
To test the endpoint without compression, turn permessage-deflate off for this request.

confirm_with: The server's handshake log for this request.

ws.compressed_without_negotiation.title: The peer sent a compressed message that was never negotiated
ws.compressed_without_negotiation.explanation: A data message arrived with RSV1 set, the permessage-deflate "compressed" bit, although the handshake negotiated no compression.{offer_note} Anvil treated it as a protocol violation by the peer and closed the session with 1002.
alternatives: The server compresses messages without negotiating permessage-deflate.
An intermediary removed the extension negotiation from the handshake but still relays the server's compressed frames.
does_not_prove: Which hop compressed the message.
That the message content itself was invalid.

remediation.text: Make the server negotiate permessage-deflate before it compresses, or stop it from compressing; check any proxy or gateway that rewrites the handshake.

confirm_with: The server's and any gateway's WebSocket logs for this session.

ws.decompression_failed.title: A compressed WebSocket message could not be decompressed
ws.decompression_failed.explanation: A permessage-deflate message from the peer was not valid DEFLATE data ({detail}). Anvil treated it as a protocol violation by the peer and closed the session with 1002.
alternatives: The peer's compressor does not follow the negotiated parameters, for example it relies on context takeover after agreeing not to.
The peer's compressor is faulty.
An intermediary modified the frames.
does_not_prove: Which hop produced the invalid data.
That earlier messages of the session were affected.

remediation.text: Check the server's permessage-deflate implementation against the negotiated parameters.
To test the endpoint without compression, turn permessage-deflate off for this request.

ws.too_large_after_decompression.title: A compressed message exceeded Anvil's limit after decompression
ws.too_large_after_decompression.explanation: A permessage-deflate message grew past Anvil's local message limit ({limit} bytes) while it was decompressed, after {compressed} compressed bytes. Anvil stopped decompressing and closed the session with 1009. The limit applies after decompression, so a small compressed message cannot expand without bound.
alternatives: The application legitimately sends large, highly compressible messages.
A decompression bomb: a small message crafted to expand enormously.
does_not_prove: That the message was corrupt or malicious.
That the peer exceeded any limit of its own.

remediation.text: If messages this large are expected, raise the WebSocket message limit for this request intentionally.

local.workload_api_unavailable.title: The SPIFFE Workload API could not be reached
local.workload_api_unavailable.explanation: Anvil needed {purpose} from the Workload API at {endpoint} ({endpoint_source}), but {rpc} failed: {answer}. Nothing was sent to the destination.
alternatives: The Workload API is not running, or listens on another path (a SPIRE agent's socket is often /run/spire/sockets/agent.sock; Ferrum Edge serves one only with FERRUM_MESH_WORKLOAD_API_ENABLED=true).
The socket's owner, group or mode does not admit the user Anvil runs as.
SPIFFE_ENDPOINT_SOCKET or the profile's endpoint names an outdated path.
does_not_prove: That the destination is unreachable or refused anything: it was never contacted.
That this process is not entitled to an identity: the Workload API never answered.

remediation.text: Check the endpoint in the profile (or SPIFFE_ENDPOINT_SOCKET), that the Workload API is running, and that its socket admits this user.
Ask the operator of the SPIRE agent or mesh proxy whether its Workload API is enabled on this host and at which path.

confirm_with: `ls -l` on the socket path and the agent's or proxy's startup log naming the socket it serves.

local.workload_api_denied.title: The Workload API issued no identity to Anvil
local.workload_api_denied.explanation: {rpc} at {endpoint} answered {answer}. A Workload API identifies its caller from the socket's peer credentials (Anvil runs as {uid}); it issued no {what} for {purpose}. Nothing was sent to the destination.
alternatives: No registration entry or attestation rule maps this user or process to a SPIFFE ID (SPIRE: a registration entry with a matching unix selector; Ferrum Edge: FERRUM_MESH_WORKLOAD_API_UNIX_IDENTITY_RULES).
The profile asks for a SPIFFE ID this workload does not hold.
The agent has not received this workload's entries yet.
does_not_prove: Why the Workload API refused: its answer does not name the rule it applied.
That the destination would reject the request: it was never contacted.

remediation.text: Ask the identity operator to register this workload ({uid}) for the intended SPIFFE ID, or select a SPIFFE ID it holds.

confirm_with: The Workload API server's log for this call (it records which workload asked and why it was refused).

local.workload_api_failed.title: The Workload API call failed
local.workload_api_failed.explanation: {rpc} at {endpoint} failed while Anvil fetched {purpose}: {answer}. Nothing was sent to the destination.
alternatives: UNIMPLEMENTED on a JWT call: this Workload API serves only X.509-SVIDs (for example a Ferrum Edge CA backend without a JWT signing authority).
INVALID_ARGUMENT: the server refused the request as malformed (for example an audience it does not accept).
The endpoint is not a SPIFFE Workload API, or its answer was cut off.
does_not_prove: That the destination refused anything: it was never contacted.

remediation.text: Check what the Workload API serves (X.509-SVIDs, JWT-SVIDs) and the request Anvil made (the profile's audiences and SPIFFE ID).

confirm_with: The Workload API server's log for this call.

auth.jwt_svid_expired.title: The JWT-SVID has expired
auth.jwt_svid_expired.explanation: The JWT-SVID's time claims fail by this machine's clock: {detail} (exp {expires}). {outcome}
alternatives: This machine's clock is ahead of the issuer's.
The token was stored in a variable or file before its issuer rotated it.
does_not_prove: That a verifier would reject it: verifiers use their own clock and clock-skew leeway.
That the token's signature is valid or invalid.

remediation.text: Use a fresh JWT-SVID (the Workload API source fetches one before it expires) and check this machine's clock.

confirm_with: The token's exp and iat claims in the record, and the verifier's clock.

auth.jwt_svid_audience_mismatch.title: The JWT-SVID is not issued for the requested audience
auth.jwt_svid_audience_mismatch.explanation: The profile requires the audience {requested}, but the JWT-SVID's aud claim is {aud}. {outcome}
alternatives: The token was issued for another verifier.
The profile's audience differs from the one the token was requested with.
does_not_prove: Which audience the verifier expects: only its configuration says.

remediation.text: Request the JWT-SVID for the verifier's audience, or correct the profile's audience.

confirm_with: The verifier's configured audience (for Ferrum Edge, the jwks_auth provider's audiences).

auth.jwt_svid_invalid.title: The JWT-SVID failed a local check
auth.jwt_svid_invalid.explanation: Anvil checked the JWT-SVID before sending it and found: {failures}. {outcome}
alternatives: The token is not a JWT-SVID (another JWT, or a truncated value).
The token was signed by a key that is not in the trust domain's current JWT bundle (a rotated or restarted issuer key).
does_not_prove: How a verifier would treat the token: only its own validation decides.

remediation.text: Use a JWT-SVID issued by the trust domain's Workload API for this workload, and compare its kid with the JWT bundle.

confirm_with: The token's header and claims in the record, and the JWT bundle from FetchJWTBundles.

auth.jwt_svid_rejected.title: The destination rejected the JWT-SVID (401)
auth.jwt_svid_rejected.explanation: {host} answered 401 to a request that carried a JWT-SVID for {subject} (aud {audiences}, expires {expires}). Anvil's local checks: {checks}. {body}
alternatives: The verifier expects a different audience than {audiences}.
The verifier trusts a different JWT bundle or key (a rotated or restarted issuer key, or another trust domain).
The verifier requires a claim JWT-SVIDs do not carry (for example an issuer or scopes).
The verifier reads the token from another header or scheme.
The token is expired or not yet valid by the verifier's clock.
Another authentication step on the path failed.
does_not_prove: Which check the verifier failed: its public answer does not identify the reason beyond its body.
Which component (gateway or application) returned the 401.

remediation.text: Compare the token's audience, subject and key id (in the record) with the verifier's configuration and JWT bundle.
Ask the verifier's operator which audience and JWT bundle it validates JWT-SVIDs against.

confirm_with: The verifier's log for this request (the reason it rejected the token).

fragments.alt.proxy_protocol.header_may_be_require: The listener may require a PROXY protocol header, which Anvil did not send: a listener with PROXY protocol enabled (for example a Ferrum Edge stream listener with stream_proxy_protocol: true, HAProxy accept-proxy or nginx listen … proxy_protocol) closes a connection that does not begin with a valid header, without sending anything back.
fragments.alt.proxy_protocol.envelope_may_be_dropp: The listener may have dropped the PROXY v2 envelope Anvil sent on each datagram. Envelope checks fail silently: an untrusted source address, an authentication tag that does not verify (wrong secret or listener identity), a sequence already used, or a timestamp outside the listener's freshness horizon.
fragments.alt.hbone.udp_refused: The endpoint does not relay a UDP (datagram) tunnel to {authority}: a mesh terminator relays one only on an inbound mesh listener, only to a destination it terminates for or an allow-listed external UDP destination, and only for an authenticated mesh peer; one without datagram-tunnel support may answer a udp-marked CONNECT with 404 or 405.
fragments.alt.hbone.udp_unavailable: The endpoint could not resolve {authority} or open its UDP socket toward it, or it is at its UDP relay session limit. UDP has no handshake, so this does not show whether anything listens at {authority}.
fragments.alt.hbone.udp_silence: The HBONE endpoint opened the tunnel, but it relays datagrams to {authority} without acknowledgement: it or the path beyond it may have dropped them, and ICMP errors toward {authority} reach the endpoint's socket, never Anvil.
fragments.alt.proxy_protocol.header_may_be_unexpec: The listener may not expect a PROXY protocol header: Anvil wrote one at the head of this new connection, and a listener without PROXY protocol reads those bytes as the start of the HTTP request or of the TLS handshake and rejects them (for example with 400 Bad Request or a TLS alert). Ferrum Edge HTTP listeners never read a PROXY header; they take the client address from X-Forwarded-For.
